about: 20 real items from Kranto's library (a copy, 2026-11-12): 10 News brief items and 10 idea cards with their sources' claims.

items.title: DeepMind releases Gemini Robotics 2.5 with Mercedes-Benz factory results
items.facts:
Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, its most capable vision-language-action model to date. It reports a 96% success rate for Apollo 2 humanoids sorting parts on Mercedes-Benz lines, and released an open safety benchmark, ASIMOV-jailbreak.
Kranto on whether general robot foundation models are moving from demos to production-line work.

items.title: Boston Dynamics puts wheels on Atlas to test whole-body control
items.facts:
Boston Dynamics released video of Atlas with scooter wheels in place of feet, a research testbed and not a product. It combines model-based control with a reinforcement-learning policy trained in simulation, and the robot performed a 360-degree jump.
Shows sim-to-real reinforcement learning being applied to humanoid whole-body control, though this is a testbed.

items.title: Amazon team's single policy grasps 66 objects with no teleoperation data
items.facts:
Amazon FAR's Dex-Hands team showed Pick Anything, one policy using a stereo camera head, no wrist cameras and Sharpa Wave hands. A researcher says it was trained on video and RL with zero teleoperation data.
Kranto on whether dexterous grasping can be trained without costly human teleoperation data.

items.title: China drafts lifetime ID codes for every robot made in the country
items.facts:
China's industry ministry (MIIT) posted a draft on Nov 6, open for comment until Dec 5. It would require a tamper-proof code on every complete robot, with makers registering products and filing codes within 20 working days.
It would extend traceability rules beyond humanoids to industrial and service robots, and it Kranto on makers selling into China.

items.title: US FCC bans new models of some connected devices, including legged robots
items.facts:
The Robot Report reports the FCC banned new models of certain connected advanced devices, including legged robots and AMRs, with Intel and Husqvarna among firms already conditionally approved. This came alongside coverage of China's block on SoftBank's ABB Robotics deal.
Kranto on whether new legged and mobile robot models can reach the US market.

items.title: China blocks SoftBank's $5.4B purchase of ABB Robotics
items.facts:
China's foreign investment security review office prohibited SoftBank Group's roughly $5.375B acquisition of ABB's robotics division, and ABB confirmed the block. The FT reports regulators feared robotics data would go overseas to train AI models.
It shows how data concerns over AI training can stop cross-border robotics deals.

items.title: LiberAI unveils Liber-0 world action model trained on human experience
items.facts:
Beijing-based LiberAI announced Liber-0, pretrained on over 2.2 million hours of human video and glove-recorded motion. It self-reports 36.0% overall success across 600 zero-shot trials, though pretraining included robot data.
Shows how far learning from human video, rather than robot demonstrations, currently gets on unseen manipulation tasks.

items.title: A3 publishes ISO 21423 for mixed-vendor mobile robot communication
items.facts:
A3 published ISO 21423:2026, developed by ISO Technical Committee 299. It sets common communication requirements for AGVs, AMRs and similar systems from different suppliers operating in the same facility.
Kranto on whether fleets from several vendors can share a site without custom integration.

items.title: Robots race up Mount Tai in China's first robot climbing competition
items.facts:
The inaugural World Robot Climbing Mount Tai Competition ended Monday in Tai'an, Shandong, with robots from more than 50 embodied AI organizations. One report says robots climbed 3,100 stone steps in 43 minutes.
It is a public test of legged-robot mobility on rough terrain, which the organizers tie to rescue and inspection work.

items.title: Bedrock Robotics raises $600M at $4.1B for working excavators
items.facts:
A weekly roundup reports Bedrock Robotics raised $600M at $4.1B for excavators already doing paid work. It also says Agility's SPAC trust is down to about $164M ahead of AGLT, and four of the top five humanoid shippers are Chinese.
Shows where robotics funding went this week and how the humanoid market is split by shipments.

items.title: Fixed-task canary that detects silent tightening of AI subscription limits and quality
items.one_liner: Existing trackers report how much of a window is used, not how much work a percent of that window buys.
items.about:
Fixed-task canary that detects silent tightening of AI subscription limits and quality
Existing trackers report how much of a window is used, not how much work a percent of that window buys.
Existing trackers report how much of a window is used, not how much work a percent of that window buys. A small canary would run the same fixed task on a schedule and log tokens, cost and a pass/fail check per percent of limit consumed. A change in that ratio would flag a silent cut in limits, a model swap or a prompt change before the user hits a wall mid-task. The pattern is borrowed from uptime and SLA monitoring, and the preconditions are frequent limit changes plus opaque meters.

items.title: Compile long single-prompt voice agents into an explicit, checkable state graph
items.one_liner: Small-business voice agents are being shipped as one giant prompt that quietly encodes a state machine, and nobody can inspect or test that machine.
items.about:
Compile long single-prompt voice agents into an explicit, checkable state graph
Small-business voice agents are being shipped as one giant prompt that quietly encodes a state machine, and nobody can inspect or test that machine.
Small-business voice agents are being shipped as one giant prompt that quietly encodes a state machine, and nobody can inspect or test that machine. A tool could read such a prompt, extract the implied states, transitions and tool calls, and flag ambiguous or conflicting instructions and unreachable steps. The owner could then keep the prompt or move to an explicit flow. The need is visible now because the single-prompt style has become the default in production deployments.

Self-hosters track versions and CVEs but have no routine signal for when a tool they depend on narrows its free tier, changes license or is wound down. items.title: Serve many structured decisions from one LLM forward pass, with a decision audit harness
items.one_liner: Standard LLM serving treats generation as the unit of work, but routing, moderation and scoring need many small decisions answered fast.
items.about:
Serve many structured decisions from one LLM forward pass, with a decision audit harness
Standard LLM serving treats generation as the unit of work, but routing, moderation and scoring need many small decisions answered fast.
Standard LLM serving treats generation as the unit of work, but routing, moderation and scoring need many small decisions answered fast. Frozen LLMs can now answer them from single-token option distributions, and serving stacks are starting to accommodate this. A thin multi-decision scoring endpoint, paired with a harness that checks the decisions for stability and asymmetry under input perturbation, would be useful before anyone trusts these cheap decisions in production.

items.title: Per-agent quotas and circuit breakers for agent-opened pull requests and CI minutes
items.one_liner: Agent-authored changes are bursty and cheap to produce.
items.about:
Per-agent quotas and circuit breakers for agent-opened pull requests and CI minutes
Agent-authored changes are bursty and cheap to produce.
Agent-authored changes are bursty and cheap to produce. Per-human assumptions in CI, review and billing break when one employee's agents open hundreds of PRs after a model release. The cost-control pattern from AI apps (hourly caps, circuit breakers, spend limits) can be applied to the pull-request pipeline: tag agent-authored PRs, give each actor a CI-minutes budget, queue the overflow, and trip a breaker on surges. Teams are only now seeing this load, so tooling built for it has little competition.

Many people now run a local LLM over thousands of texts for a fixed labeling or extraction task, which is slow and needs a GPU. A tool could take the local LLM's labels on a sample, train an embedding plus logistic regression model (or a small encoder) on them, and report how closely it agrees with the LLM and how much faster it runs. The pieces are already shown separately: local LLM labeling, cheap classifiers near SOTA, and encoder versus local-LLM latency measurements. Nobody in these observations has packaged them into a workflow for the local-LLM user.

items.title: Placebo-controlled effectiveness and conflict checks for community Claude Code skills
items.one_liner: A registry of one million skills makes choosing among them the bottleneck.
items.about:
Placebo-controlled effectiveness and conflict checks for community Claude Code skills
A registry of one million skills makes choosing among them the bottleneck.
A registry of one million skills makes choosing among them the bottleneck. The one placebo-controlled trial found most popular skills indistinguishable from neutral text, and a mining study found a very large number of similar-skill pairs that can silently compete. A local tool that tests the skills a person actually has installed against a placebo of equal length, and flags description overlap between them, would apply a known vetting pattern to a registry that has grown faster than anyone can judge it.
